item: both problems via personalized generation of plausible, user-specific recipes using user preferences extracted from previously consumed recipes
two important tasks from natural language processing and recommender systems: data-to-text generation and personalized recommendation
the name of a specific dish, a few key ingredients, and a calorie level
these loose input specifications to an encoder-decoder framework
it for the problem of recipe generation
a new task of generating plausible and personalized recipes from incomplete input specifications by leveraging historical user preferences
a new dataset of 180K+ recipes and 700K+ user reviews for this task
new evaluation strategies for generation quality in instructional texts
procedurally structured recipes instead of free-form narratives
recipes as a structured collection of ingredient entities acted upon by cooking actions
a `checklist' attention constraint emphasizing hitherto unused ingredients during generation
explicit ingredient references in the prior recipe step
Similar hierarchical approaches that infer a full ingredient list to constrain generation
our setting due to the potentially unconstrained number of ingredients (from a space of 10K+) in a recipe
historical preferences to guide full recipe generation
historical user preferences from previously consumed recipes to generate recipe content, rather than writing styles
the recipe name as a sequence of tokens, a partial list of ingredients, and a caloric level (high, medium, low)
the recipe instructions as a token sequence: $\mathcal {W}_r=\lbrace w_{r,0}, \dots , w_{r,T}\rbrace $ for a recipe $r$ of length $T$
historical recipe interactions of a user $u \in \mathcal {U}$
three embedding layers: vocabulary embedding $\mathcal {V}$, ingredient embedding $\mathcal {I}$, and caloric-level embedding $\mathcal {C}$
Each token in the (length $L_n$) recipe name
set of prior recipes for a user $u$
the attention by the user's prior technique preference
a novel dataset of 230K+ recipe texts and 1M+ user interactions (reviews) over 18 years (2000-2018) from Food.com
recipes with at least 3 steps, and at least 4 and no more than 20 ingredients
the first 3-5 ingredients listed in each recipe
compute the likelihood of generated recipes using
identical input specifications but conditioned on ten different user profiles
the neural scoring model from BIBREF33 to measure recipe-level coherence for each generated recipe
average recipe-level coherence scores of 1.78-1.82, surpassing the baseline at 1.77
an entailment task: predicting the likelihood that a recipe step follows the preceding
